item.title: Amazon to invest $7 billion in India's renewable energy projects by 2030
item.description: Amazon on Tuesday announced plans to invest USD 7 billion (about Rs 65,393 crore) in renewable energy projects in India by 2030, in addition to the USD 4 billion already contracted, as it unveiled four new wind and solar projects with a combined capacity of 934 megawatts. The company said the investment makes it one of India's leading corporate purchasers of carbon-free energy. The four initiatives consist of a 234 MW wind farm in Karnataka -- marking Amazon's largest contracted wind project in Asia to date -- alongside a 200 MW hybrid solar-and-wind facility in the same state, a 300 MW solar installation in Madhya Pradesh, and a 200 MW solar project in Rajasthan. Secured through power purchase agreements (PPAs), the projects are part of the USD 4 billion in renewable energy projects already contracted by Amazon in India, the company said. item.title: Anil Agarwal warns Vedanta block transfer to ONGC could deter investors
item.description: Mining czar Anil Agarwal on Tuesday warned that the government's decision to transfer operations of a producing offshore oil and gas block from his company to state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) could send wrong signal to investors. In a LinkedIn post, he urged policymakers to maintain regulatory stability and avoid disrupting existing operators. "Recently, our running field has been given to ONGC which will send a very wrong signal to investors," he said, referring to the disputed Cambay offshore block in Gujarat that ONGC took over from Vedanta in July following a Delhi High Court ruling. Agarwal said Vedanta Oil and Gas, which he described as India's largest private-sector producer, was committing USD 5 billion to scale up production to between 300,000 and 500,000 barrels per day. item.title: DP World launches export rail service linking NCR to Mundra Port for ONE
item.description: Global logistics operator DP World has launched a dedicated export rail freight service for Ocean Network Express (ONE), connecting exporters in the National Capital Region (NCR) to Mundra Port, the company said on Monday. Operating on the Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC), the twice-weekly export service provides scheduled rail departures with a capacity of up to 180 TEUs per run, is aligned with vessel schedules to provide better coordination between inland cargo movements and ocean shipping services, helping exporters manage shipments with greater confidence and flexibility, DP World said. By linking inland cargo hubs directly with the port, the service enables exporters to move cargo more efficiently, improve planning and gain more predictable access to global markets, it said. The service supports multiple commodities within a single rake, providing customers across the connected regions with dedicated rail capacity, it added. item.title: Tata Steel eyes 50 MT capacity, to direct 75% capex to India: TV Narendran
item.description: Tata Steel is targeting an ambitious expansion of its annual steelmaking capacity in India to 50 million tonnes over the next decade and is exploring the possibility of setting up a 15 MT greenfield plant in Maharashtra, as it seeks to capitalise on the country's growing steel demand, Managing Director and CEO T V Narendran said. The company, which currently has an annual capacity of around 27 million tonnes, believes its existing manufacturing facilities can support expansion to 50 million tonnes, while Maharashtra could emerge as a major growth destination beyond its ongoing projects. "We have a roadmap for 40 MT. We also know that the existing facilities can go up to 50 MT, so that is clear. The path is available. It is up to us how fast we can move," Narendran said in an interview. "We are constantly looking five years, 10 years ahead. How do we create a pathway so that we can grow fast? item.title: TVS' Lakshmi Venu seeks partition of family assets, escalating family feud
item.description: Lakshmi Venu, a member of the TVS industrial family, has formally sought a partition of the joint family assets of her father Venu Srinivasan's branch, escalating a succession dispute that could have implications for ownership and control of key businesses within one of India's best-known automobile groups. In a partition notice to her father, Lakshmi called on him, as head of the family, to discharge his fiduciary duties and ensure a "fair and lawful partition," according to a statement from her office on Monday. Her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, has publicly backed her claim, exposing a deepening rift within the family over the distribution of its wealth. Lakshmi maintains that she is entitled to an equal share under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, and has an independent right to seek partition.
